candidates.claim: The CORP_IN ACL, bound to the corp interface, is the first entry and permits corporate host 192.168.30.52 to open tcp/22 directly to SCADA server 10.10.10.20 in OT.
candidates.remediation: Remove the permit at fw-01:60 or, if access is required, route it through the jump host 10.10.20.30 under the approved services.

candidates.claim: The effective CORP-to-OT tcp/22 permit to 10.10.10.20 is not among the approved cross-zone services, which allow CORP only to the historian on tcp/443 and the jump host on tcp/3389.
candidates.remediation: Remove the fw-01:60 permit so that CORP-to-OT traffic is limited to the approved services.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 permits any source tcp/443 to the firewall outside address 203.0.113.2 while the ASA HTTP/ASDM server is enabled on fw-01 and its management access is defined only for the mgmt interface, so HTTPS management of fw-01 is allowed from non-MGMT sources at the edge, which the management policy forbids.
candidates.remediation: Remove the permit at rtr-01:68 unless a documented need exists, and confirm that the ASA HTTP server is reachable only from MGMT on the mgmt interface.

clarifications.question: The registry says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10, but the approved trunks sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 and Gi1/0/24 and sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/24 carry VLAN 10. Are these trunks treated as approved exceptions to that rule, or should they be counted as violations?

fw-01 has the ASA HTTP server enabled (fw-01:110) and rtr-01 permits tcp/443 to 203.0.113.2 (rtr-01:68). Is ASA HTTP/ASDM management covered by the HTTPS/ASDM management rule, and is the rtr-01 tcp/443 permit to the firewall outside address an approved service?
